uncited: **Inputs:** Camera position $(C_x, C_y, C_z)$, render distance $R$, and a hash map $H$ mapping chunk coordinates to chunk objects.
**Outputs:** A set of chunks to render and an updated hash map $H$.
*   **Hash Map $H$:** Maps 3D integer coordinates $(cx, cy, cz)$ to `Chunk` pointers.
**Iterate and Load:** Iterate through all integer chunk coordinates $(cx, cy, cz)$ within the AoI bounds.
*   If $(cx, cy, cz)$ exists in $H$, fetch the chunk object.
*   If $(cx, cy, cz)$ does not exist in $H$, create a new chunk object, insert it into $H$, and fetch it.
**Unload:** Identify all chunks in $H$ whose coordinates lie outside the AoI.
An optimization where sub-chunks (smaller subdivisions within a chunk) are culled when the camera is underground.
**Time Complexity:** $O(V)$ where $V$ is the number of voxels in the AoI, assuming constant-time hash map lookups and chunk creation.
Unloading is $O(C)$ where $C$ is the number of active chunks.
**Memory Complexity:** Proportional to the number of chunks within the AoI.
**Strengths:** Simple implementation; effective memory management for large worlds.
**Limitations:** Requires custom hash map handling for 3D coordinates; potential for frequent allocation/deallocation if camera moves erratically.
It builds on the chunk-based world storage model [2858-chunk-based-world-storage.md].
